What you are preparing for
DHET Installation Rules Examination
Programme No. 51108848

The Installation Rules examination is administered by the Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET) under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system. It qualifies you as a competent person in terms of SANS 10142-1 (Wiring of Premises). Two 3-hour national papers are written, each carrying 100 marks and 10 questions. Pass mark: 50%. A score of 75% or more on a single paper earns permanent exemption from that paper; the second paper must be passed within 12 months. No condonation applies.

T880 · Paper 1 · Code 11040412
Legislation, Regulations & Theory
10 questions · 100 marks
Q1OHS Act 85 of 1993 — Sections 1, 8, 9, 10, 22 (definitions, employer/employee duties, HSRs, incident notification) Q2Electrical Installation Regulations (EIR) — Regulations 1 to 14 (competent persons, CoC obligations, testing) Q3Electrical Machinery Regulations (EMR) — Regulations 1, 3, 5, 6, 11 (scope, general safety, maintenance) Q4Construction Regulations — Regulation 22 (temporary electrical installations on construction sites) Q5SANS 10142-1:2008 — Sections 1, 2, 3 (scope, normative references, definitions) Q6SANS 10142-1:2008 — Sections 4, 5 (general requirements, circuit design) Q7SANS 10142-1:2008 — Section 7 + Annexures D, F, G (installation methods; discharge lamps; suspended ceilings; inspection & testing) Q8SANS 10142-1:2008 — Annexures J, M, P, Q (ELV systems; medical locations; Form of Approval; installation test report) Q9SANS 10198-1:2004 and SANS 10198-2:2004 — overhead power lines (no calculations required on SANS 10198-2) Q10SANS 10292:2001 — earthing of LV distribution systems; installation testing; switchgear assemblies
⚠ Indicative Q-by-Q allocation only — exact question topics vary per sitting. DHET Examination Instruction 08 of 2009 defines syllabus scope per paper, not per question. SANS 10313 is NOT a Paper 1 syllabus item.
T890 · Paper 2 · Code 11040432
Sections 6 & 8 — Earthing, Conductors & Special Locations
10 questions · 100 marks
Q1SANS 10142-1:2008 Section 6 — earthing systems: general requirements, earth electrodes, earth electrode resistance Q2SANS 10142-1:2008 Section 6 — protective bonding, earth fault loop impedance, fault protection, residual current devices Q3SANS 10142-1:2008 Section 8 — conductor selection, current-carrying capacity, correction factors, voltage drop Q4SANS 10142-1:2008 Section 8 — wiring systems, cables, flexible cords, installation methods Q5SANS 10142-1:2008 Annexure B — [verify content against SANS 10142-1:2008] Q6SANS 10142-1:2008 Annexure C — [verify content against SANS 10142-1:2008] Q7SANS 10142-1:2008 Annexure E — [verify content against SANS 10142-1:2008] Q8SANS 10142-1:2008 Annexures K, L — [verify content against SANS 10142-1:2008] Q9SANS 10142-1:2008 Annexures N, O — [verify content against SANS 10142-1:2008] Q10SANS 1973-3:2008 — surge protective devices (SPDs) for LV electrical installations
⚠ Q5–Q9 annexure content descriptions require manual verification against SANS 10142-1:2008. Indicative Q-by-Q allocation only — exact question topics vary per sitting.
What comes after Installation Rules?

Once you hold both Paper 1 (11040412) and Paper 2 (11040432) passes for the Installation Rules programme, you qualify to register as an Installation Electrician (IE) with the Department of Employment and Labour (DoEL) under the OHS Act.

The Specialised Electrical Installation Codes (Programme No. 51108849) are the next examination series. Passing those two papers allows registration as a Master Installation Electrician (MIE), which authorises work in hazardous and classified locations. The Specialised Codes are covered in a separate study companion and are not in scope here.

SANS 10142-1 — History & Edition Progression
1922Factory Act — first statutory electrical safety provisions for premises installations in South Africa 1940SAIEE Red Code — first South African Electrical Wiring Code, published by the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers (SAIEE) 1952SAIEE Blue Code — revised wiring code 1978SAIEE Green Code — major revision, widely adopted across industry 2001SABS 0142:2001 "Grey Code" — last edition under SABS 0142 numbering system 2003SANS 10142-1 Ed 1.1 — "Black Folder"; first edition under SANS numbering; legislative force via OHS Act 85 of 1993 and Electrical Installation Regulations 2012SANS 10142-1 Ed 1.8 — final amendment of the Edition 1.x series (Editions 1.1 through 1.8) 2017SANS 10142-1 Ed 2 — comprehensive revision; improved circuit design, earthing & certificate of compliance provisions 2020SANS 10142-1 Ed 3 — ~20 Working Group meetings, ~3½ years in development; expanded scope including small-scale embedded generation (SSEG) 2021Ed 3.1 (Amendment 1) — first amendment to Edition 3 2024Ed 3.2 (Amendment 2) — Part 1-1 (medical locations) and Part 1-2 (SSEG connected in parallel to LV distribution systems) formally subdivided 2026Ed 3.3 (Amendment 3, June 2026) — supersedes Ed 3.2; new generating-plant (GP / PV-battery) annex and installation test report added; 12-month parallel transition window for existing test-report forms
Sources: SAIEE Archives; SANS 10142-1:2026 Ed 3.3; SABS publication records. Note: the DHET examination currently references SANS 10142-1:2008 — exam papers test that edition, not Edition 3.

Reference
Basic Electrical Formulae
Ohm's Law
V = I × R
V = volts · I = amps · R = ohms
Power
P = V × I = I²R
P = watts · also P = V²/R
Voltage Drop
Vd = I × (mVA/m × L) / 1000
SANS 10142-1 max 5% (2.5% preferred)
Fault Loop Impedance
Zs = Ze + (R1 + R2)
Ze = external · R1+R2 = conductors
Prospective Fault Current
If = Uo / Zs
Uo = nominal voltage to earth (230 V)
Resistance of Conductor
R = ρL / A
ρ = resistivity · L = length · A = area mm²
Scenario-Based Formula Practice
Scenario A — Cable sizing (voltage drop)

A 15 A circuit, 25 m long, using 2.5 mm² copper (mV/A/m = 18). Permitted Vd = 11.5 V.

Vd = 15 × 18 × 25 / 1000 = 6.75 V ✓ (within limit)
Scenario B — Fault loop impedance

Ze = 0.35 Ω · 20 m of 2.5 mm² live (R1=0.18 Ω/m/100m=0.036 Ω) and 1.5 mm² CPC (R2=0.3 Ω). Find Zs and If.

Zs = 0.35 + 0.036 + 0.3 = 0.686 Ω · If = 230/0.686 = 335 A
Scenario C — Power calculation

A 230 V, 13 A appliance. Find power, and resistance when hot.

P = 230×13 = 2 990 W ≈ 3 kW · R = 230/13 = 17.7 Ω
